meta.title: Renew your ADA certification
meta.description: How to renew your ADA doula certification: a certification period of {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}, a {fee} renewal fee, and a choice of reference letters or a recertification exam.

title: Renew your ADA certification
lead: Renew before your certification period ends and you stay in good standing. To begin, contact ADA.

need.title: What you need
need.photoAlt: An instructor teaching a newborn-care lesson beside a slide, with training dolls on the table
need.photoCaption: A newborn-care lesson in the ADA Postpartum Doula Program. August 2024.
need.doulaIdValue: In the form <nowrap>#YY-NNNN</nowrap>. It is on your original certificate.
need.emailValue: The email address ADA has on file for you.
need.pathwayValue: Pathway A, professional reference letters, or Pathway B, the recertification exam. <link>Compare the pathways</link>

pathways.title: Renewal pathways
pathways.intro: Choose the one that works best for you. Each shows ADA that you are still practicing well.
pathways.caption: The ADA renewal pathways
pathways.aWhat: Submit {count} professional reference letters from clients, colleagues or healthcare professionals who can speak to your work as a doula.
pathways.aItem1: The full name of the reference
pathways.aItem2: A phone number or email address
pathways.aItem3: A written recommendation describing your doula work
pathways.bWhat: Take a shorter recertification exam to show your continued competency in postpartum doula care.
pathways.bItem1: Shorter than the initial certification exam

steps.title: How to renew
steps.s1Body: Check your current status and expiration date in the ADA registry, or sign in to your doula portal. You need your Doula ID, in the form <nowrap>#YY-NNNN</nowrap>, and your registered email address.
steps.s2Body: Pathway A, professional reference letters, or Pathway B, the recertification exam. <link>Compare the pathways</link>
steps.s3Body: Send your renewal application with your pathway materials (reference letters or exam results) and the {fee} renewal fee.
steps.s4Body: Once ADA reviews and approves your application, you receive your renewed certification, valid for another {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}} from the renewal date.
steps.s4Item2: Your verification status, updated in the ADA registry and your doula portal

status.title: What your record shows
status.intro: Families, insurers and agencies check your public record in the ADA registry, so it always shows your current standing. Each credential on it carries one of these statuses.
status.active: Meets ADA certification requirements through the date shown.
status.superseded: An older certificate replaced by a newer one, usually at renewal.
status.expired: Was certified, but not renewed by the end date. Not currently ADA-certified. This is not a disciplinary action.
status.suspended: Not ADA-certified for a set period under the Code of Conduct.
status.revoked: Certification withdrawn under the Code of Conduct.

cta.title: Ready to renew? Contact ADA to begin.
